content:
The test image shows a corn plant with complete whole-plant wilting and browning — all leaves dried/tan while surrounding plants are healthy green. This "dead plant in green field" pattern points to a wilt or stalk disease.

Top candidates: Goss's Wilt, Stewart's Disease, Bacterial Stalk Rot.

Let me check a Goss's Wilt reference image.

The Goss's Wilt reference shows leaf lesions with tan/brown streaking but the plant isn't fully dead. The test image shows a more advanced stage — complete whole-plant collapse with all leaves uniformly tan/brown and wilted, while surrounding plants are fully healthy.

This complete whole-plant "firing" (all leaves brown, plant standing dead) is a hallmark of Goss's Wilt at advanced stage, or Stewart's Disease wilt phase. The uniform browning across all leaves without ear rot or specific lesion patterns points more toward a bacterial wilt. Goss's Wilt is known for this rapid whole-plant death and "leaf firing" appearance.
